cards.text: This is a song of David, Israel's king, written for the choirmaster. David is crying out to God. Pull up a stool, friend.

cards.question: David is crying out to God in a song for the choirmaster. What does he ask for first?

answers.text: That God hurry to help him
That God show him the way to go

cards.text: “Hurry, O LORD, to help me!” That's the prayer version of mashing the elevator button five times, and honestly? I RESPECT it. Then David turns to the people who seek his life.

cards.question: David prays that the people who seek his life will end up ashamed.

cards.text: Then there are the ones who say, “Aha, aha!” That's the sound of somebody watching you drop a whole tray of cookies and LAUGHING about it. David prays they retreat because of their shame.

cards.question: David turns from his enemies to a different crowd: everyone who seeks God. What does he want for them?

answers.text: That they rejoice and be glad in God
That they hide until the danger passes
That they march out and fight beside him

cards.text: Then David looks at himself and says, “But I am poor and needy” and this is the KING of Israel. Meanwhile I put on a clean apron and strut around like I own the planet.

cards.question: David calls himself poor and needy, but he says God is his help and his ___.
David closes Psalm 70 by telling God to take His time.

cards.text: Psalm 71 is a new prayer, and it doesn't name who wrote it, so we'll just call him the psalmist. He starts, “In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.”

cards.question: The psalmist asks God to rescue and deliver him. What does he appeal to?

cards.text: He wants God to be his rock of refuge, a place he can always go. Not a place with business hours, friend. ALWAYS.

cards.question: The psalmist asks God to save him because he's earned it with his good deeds.
The psalmist asks God to deliver him from the hand of the ___ and from the grasp of the unjust and ruthless.

cards.text: Then he looks back. Way back. God has been his hope and his confidence from his youth.

cards.question: The psalmist has trusted God from his youth. But how far back does his leaning on God really go?
The psalmist says he has become a portent to many, and it has pushed him away from God.
All day long, the psalmist's mouth is filled with God's ___.

cards.text: Now the psalmist prays about getting older: “Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.” Discard? Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, I KNOW that word.

cards.question: The psalmist's enemies are plotting against him. What do they say about him?

cards.text: And they don't stop at talk. They say, “pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”

cards.question: With his enemies saying no one will rescue him, the psalmist asks God not to be far from him.

cards.text: He prays, “Hurry, O my God, to help me,” so we're right back to mashing the elevator button. Then he asks that his accusers be covered with scorn and disgrace.

cards.question: With accusers all around, the psalmist says he'll go quiet and wait it out.
The psalmist says he'll tell of God's righteousness and salvation all day long. What does he admit about them?

answers.text: He can't know their full measure
He has only seen them once
He has forgotten most of them

cards.question: The psalmist says he'll come in his own strength.

cards.text: He'll proclaim God's righteousness, “Yours alone,” he says. God has taught him from his youth, and to this day he's still telling of God's marvelous deeds.

cards.question: The psalmist asks God not to forsake him, even when he's old and gray. Until what?

answers.text: Until he tells the next generation of God's power
Until every one of his enemies is gone
Until he gets to see his home once more

cards.text: He wants to tell God's might to all who are to come. Most folks pray for retirement, but this man is praying for OVERTIME.
Then he looks UP. God's righteousness, he says, reaches to the heavens, and God has done great things. Friend, my tallest cookie stack barely reaches my hat.

cards.question: Thinking of the great things God has done, the psalmist asks God a question. What is it?

answers.text: How long will this go on

cards.text: Then he gets honest: God has shown him many troubles and misfortunes.

cards.question: After all those troubles and misfortunes, the psalmist says God will ___ him once again.

cards.text: Even from the depths of the earth, he says, God will bring him back up. Friend, I know a little something about being brought up out of the dark, even if mine was just a junk drawer.

cards.question: The psalmist says God will increase his honor and comfort him once again.
The psalmist says he'll praise God with the harp and the lyre. What does he praise God for?
When the psalmist sings, his lips shout for joy along with his soul, which God has ___.

cards.text: He wraps up the way he promised, telling of God's righteousness all day long. And the ones who wanted to harm him? Disgraced and confounded.

That points to something earlier than youth. "Since his first battle" and "Since his wedding day" both come after youth, so only "Since birth" is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
